sections.title: Authority
sections.body: These rules govern the procedures and voting thresholds of the Assembly. They may be amended only by referendum of the full membership. The Assembly may not alter its own rules.
sections.rationale: Preventing the Assembly from changing its own voting rules eliminates a common path to institutional capture. If a majority wants to change how decisions are made, they must convince the broader membership.

sections.title: Quorum
sections.body: A quorum of two-thirds (2/3) of seated Assembly members must be present for any vote to proceed. Votes taken without quorum are void.
sections.rationale: High quorum requirements prevent small factions from making decisions when most members are absent.

sections.title: Simple Majority
sections.body: The following motions require a simple majority (more than half of votes cast) to pass: (1) routine administrative decisions, (2) policy recommendations, (3) committee appointments, (4) procedural motions.
sections.rationale: Most day-to-day Assembly business should not require supermajorities, which can create gridlock.

sections.title: Two-Thirds Majority
sections.body: The following motions require a two-thirds (2/3) majority of votes cast to pass: (1) budget appropriations, (2) amendments to the Charter, (3) creation or dissolution of Services, (4) changes to membership dues, (5) referral of questions to referendum.
sections.rationale: Decisions with significant fiscal or structural impact require broader consensus than routine matters.

sections.title: Three-Quarters Majority
sections.body: The following motions require a three-quarters (3/4) majority of votes cast to pass: (1) amendments to the Constitution, (2) emergency actions that bypass normal procedures.
sections.rationale: The highest threshold is reserved for fundamental changes to the community's structure or emergency measures that could be abused.
